```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
# the model executables are compiled for Windows: simulations are run only there
run_model <- identical(.Platform$OS.type, "windows")
```

R3DFEM is an R wrapper of the [3D-CMCC-FEM](https://www.forest-modelling-lab.com/the-3d-cmcc-model),
a bio-geochemical, process-based forest model that simulates carbon, water and nitrogen
fluxes and stocks of homogeneous and heterogeneous forests. The package provides
functions to:

1. create and check the input files of the model;
2. run the model (versions 5.6 and 5.7) from R;
3. plot inputs and outputs.

This vignette walks through the whole workflow using the example data shipped with the
package.

```{r load}
library(R3DFEM)
```

The package can be installed from GitHub with
`devtools::install_github("VangiElia/R3DFEM")`. Due to storage limits, the E-OBS climate
data and the SoilGrids raster used by `make_meteo_EOBS_30.0()`, `make_meteo_EOBS()` and
`make_soil_ISRIC()` are not stored on GitHub: these functions work only if the files are
copied in the `extdata` folder of the installed package.

## Input files

A simulation needs the following .txt files, all stored in the same directory and named
after the site (here `BilyKriz`) or the species:

| File | Content | Helper |
|---|---|---|
| `site_stand.txt` | initial stand: species, age, number of trees, DBH, height per class | `make_stand()` |
| `site_meteo.txt` | daily weather | `make_meteo()`, `make_meteo_EOBS_30.0()` |
| `site_co2.txt` | yearly atmospheric CO2 concentration | `make_co2()`, `make_CCS()` |
| `site_soil.txt` | soil texture and depth | `make_soil()`, `make_soil_ISRIC()` |
| `site_topo.txt` | elevation | `make_topo()` |
| `site_management.txt` | management events (only with `man = "var"`) | `make_management()` |
| `Species.txt` | species parameterization | `read_species()`, `set_species_param()` |

The package contains complete input sets for three sites (Bily Kriz, Hyytiälä and Sorø):

```{r example-data}
bk <- system.file("extdata", "bilykriz", "rcp0p0", package = "R3DFEM")
list.files(bk)
```

### Creating the input files

All the helpers write the file in `outdir` and return the data invisibly. Here we build a
new input set for Bily Kriz in a temporary directory.

```{r inputs}
inputdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "BilyKriz")

# stand: two cohorts of Norway spruce in 1997
make_stand("BilyKriz", year = 1997, age = c(16, 30), species = "Piceaabies",
           n_trees = c(2000, 300), avdbh = c(7.1, 18), height = c(5.6, 14),
           outdir = inputdir)

# soil, topography
make_soil("BilyKriz", lat = 49.3, lon = 18.32, clay = 20.63, silt = 20.63,
          sand = 58.74, soil_depth = 80, outdir = inputdir)
make_topo("BilyKriz", elev = 875, outdir = inputdir)

# CO2: known values linearly interpolated over the simulated years
make_co2("BilyKriz", years = 1997:2030,
         co2 = data.frame(year = c(1997, 2020, 2030), CO2_ppm = c(363, 412, 435)),
         outdir = inputdir)

# management (used with man = "var"): thinning and final harvest
make_management("BilyKriz", thinning = c(2005, 2015), thinning_int = c(20, 20),
                harvesting = 2025, outdir = inputdir)
```

The meteo file can be created from any daily data.frame (e.g. a weather station) with
`make_meteo()`, which computes the mean temperature if missing, converts the radiation
from W m^-2^ to MJ m^-2^ day^-1^ (`rad_unit = "W"`) and checks the result with
`check_meteo_3DFEM()`:

```{r meteo}
station <- read.delim(file.path(bk, "BilyKriz_meteo.txt"))
station <- subset(station, Year <= 2030)
station <- data.frame(date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-%02d", station$Year, station$Month, station$n_days)),
                      Rg_f = station$Rg_f, Tmax = station$Tmax, Tmin = station$Tmin,
                      Precip = station$Precip, RH_f = station$RH_f, WS_f = station$WS_f)
head(station, 3)
meteo <- make_meteo(station, "BilyKriz", rad_unit = "MJ", outdir = inputdir)
```

For European sites, the weather and the soil texture can be taken from E-OBS and
SoilGrids (data not distributed on GitHub):

```{r eobs, eval = FALSE}
plot <- data.frame(x = 18.32, y = 49.3)
make_meteo_EOBS_30.0(plot, crs = 4326, daterange = c("1997-01-01", "2023-12-31"),
                     site = "BilyKriz", outdir = inputdir)
make_soil_ISRIC(plot, crs = 4326, site = "BilyKriz", outdir = inputdir)
```

### Species parameters

The species file is copied from the example data. The version 5.7 of the model needs the
parameter `CONV_VOL_FACTOR`, so we use the 5.7 parameterization of Norway spruce in
`extdata/species_5.7` (the species files in the site folders are parameterized for the
version 5.6). `read_species()` reads the parameters, while `set_species_param()` changes
them keeping comments and order of the file (it can also write a new file with
`outfile`):

```{r species}
sp57 <- system.file("extdata", "species_5.7", package = "R3DFEM")
file.copy(file.path(sp57, "Piceaabies.txt"), inputdir)
sp <- read_species(file.path(inputdir, "Piceaabies.txt"))
head(sp)
old <- set_species_param(file.path(inputdir, "Piceaabies.txt"), LIGHT_TOL = 4)
old
```

### Checking the inputs

`check_inputs()` performs the same consistency checks of the run functions (files,
years, management and replanting options) without running the model:

```{r check}
check_inputs("BilyKriz", "Piceaabies", year_start = 1997, year_end = 2030,
             man = "off", inputdir = inputdir, version = "5.7")
```

For example, with `man = "var"` the harvest of 2025 requires the replanting arguments:

```{r check-error, error = TRUE}
check_inputs("BilyKriz", "Piceaabies", year_start = 1997, year_end = 2030,
             man = "var", pres_dens = "on", after_pres = "on", inputdir = inputdir)
```

With a 5.6 species file (without `CONV_VOL_FACTOR`) the same check stops with an error,
before running the model:

```{r check-version, error = TRUE}
old_sp <- file.path(tempdir(), "sp56")
dir.create(old_sp)
file.copy(list.files(inputdir, full.names = TRUE), old_sp)
file.copy(file.path(bk, "Piceaabies.txt"), old_sp, overwrite = TRUE)
check_inputs("BilyKriz", "Piceaabies", year_start = 1997, year_end = 2030,
             man = "off", inputdir = old_sp, version = "5.7")
```

## Running the model

`run_3DCMCCFEM()` runs the 5.6 executable, `run_3DCMCCFEM_5.7()` the 5.7 one (which adds
options like `cold_accl`, `n_reg`, `thinning_regime`, the replanting of more species and a
separate output of the management); both have the same main arguments. The settings file
is written in `inputdir`; the outputs are saved in `outputdir` (a sub-directory `output`
is created if needed) and their paths are returned invisibly. Note that the model cannot
write files whose full path is longer than 260 characters: use short output directories.

```{r run, eval = run_model}
outdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "sim")

# no management
out_off <- run_3DCMCCFEM_5.7(site = "BilyKriz", species = "Piceaabies",
                             year_start = 1997, year_end = 2030, man = "off",
                             output = "annual", inputdir = inputdir,
                             outputdir = file.path(outdir, "off"))
basename(out_off)

# management from site_management.txt, with replanting after the harvest
out_var <- run_3DCMCCFEM_5.7(site = "BilyKriz", species = "Piceaabies",
                             year_start = 1997, year_end = 2030,
                             man = "var", pres_dens = "on", after_pres = "on",
                             rep_species = "Piceaabies", rep_trees = 2000, rep_age = 3,
                             rep_dbh = 1, rep_lai = 1, rep_height = 1.3,
                             output = "annual", inputdir = inputdir,
                             outputdir = file.path(outdir, "var"))
```

## Plotting

`plot_output_3DFEM()` plots one or more output variables (with an optional rolling mean),
or one variable against another:

```{r plot-output, eval = run_model, fig.height = 5}
plot_output_3DFEM(out_var[1], y = c("GPP", "NPP", "LIVETREE", "DBH"), text_size = 14)
plot_output_3DFEM(out_off[1], y = "GPP", window = 5, text_size = 14)
```

Input files can be plotted too:

```{r plot-inputs, fig.height = 5, eval = requireNamespace("plotrix", quietly = TRUE)}
plot_meteo_3DFEM(file.path(inputdir, "BilyKriz_meteo.txt"),
                 var = c("Tmax", "Tmin", "Precip"),
                 daterange = c("2000-01-01", "2002-12-31"), window = 30)
plot_soil_3DFEM(file.path(inputdir, "BilyKriz_soil.txt"), pch = 21, bg.symbols = "red", cex = 2)
```

## Climate scenarios and virtual stands

`make_CCS()` creates a detrended "current climate scenario" by resampling the observed
years (leap years with leap years) up to `end_year`:

```{r ccs}
make_CCS(meteo = file.path(inputdir, "BilyKriz_meteo.txt"),
         co2 = file.path(inputdir, "BilyKriz_co2.txt"),
         obs_year = c(1997, 2020), end_year = 2100,
         outdir = file.path(tempdir(), "ccs"))
```

`virtual_stand_generator()` simulates the stand development and writes stand files for
age classes that are not observed, which can be used as starting points of new
simulations:

```{r virtual, eval = FALSE}
virtual_stand_generator(site = "BilyKriz", species = "Piceaabies",
                        stand_age = c(40, 60), man = "off",
                        inputdir = inputdir, outputdir = file.path(tempdir(), "virtual"))
```

## References

R3DFEM: an R package for running the 3D-CMCC-FEM model. *Earth Science Informatics*
(2025). <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12145-025-01956-0>

The model User Guide, with the full description of inputs and outputs, is available on the
[Forest Modelling Lab web page](https://www.forest-modelling-lab.com/the-3d-cmcc-model).
